name: Lacuna Fund RFP: Use Lacuna Fund's open datasets (SDG dataset utilization)
funder: Lacuna Fund (secretariat: ACTS AI Institute; multi-donor)
amount: See website (amount not stated on apply page)
eligibility: Global South teams (non-profits, research institutions/universities, social enterprises) to train, scale and apply ML models using Lacuna Fund datasets
eligibility_note: Apply page: 'Funding is available for Global South teams'; Fund focuses on 'low- and middle-income contexts globally'. No country list published on page.
how_to_apply_tip: Deadline is in 2 weeks: apply through your university (institutional applicant), name a specific Lacuna dataset (e.g. language/health/agri) you will build models on, and stress SDG impact in Pakistan/South Asia.

name: Transformative AI Fund (successor to Long-Term Future Fund)
amount: Typically USD 10,000-150,000; rarely above USD 300,000
eligibility: Individuals, new and existing organisations; technical AI safety research, policy, forecasting, field-building, training
eligibility_note: Official page states no country restriction and funds individuals; Long-Term Future Fund is closed and replaced by this fund.
how_to_apply_tip: Short online form (<1h). Frame a concrete 6-12 month AI safety project (e.g. interpretability/evals) with a modest budget; small, well-scoped asks from early-career researchers are common.

name: Foresight Institute AI for Science & Safety Grants (Nodes RFP)
amount: Typically USD 30,000-100,000 (larger possible); overhead up to 10%
eligibility: Individuals, teams, non-profits and for-profits; AI safety, local compute, coordination/accountability, AI-first science; outputs must be open-sourced
eligibility_note: RFP page lists no nationality/citizenship restriction; priority to applicants who will be in-person in SF or Berlin hubs; due diligence required.
how_to_apply_tip: Current round closes 31 Oct 2026 (23:59 PDT); if missed, watch foresight.org/grants for the next RFP. Remote applicants should explain how they will engage with the hubs.

name: Cooperative AI Foundation Research Grants (incl. Early-Career Track)
amount: Min GBP 10,000; early-career track up to GBP 100,000; past grants GBP 10k-385k
duration: Up to 12 months (early-career track); up to 2 years (standard)
eligibility: Researchers anywhere; early-career track for postdocs/junior researchers typically within 2-3 years of PhD; projects in cooperative AI research areas
eligibility_note: Grants page: 'applicants can be located anywhere in the world'; affiliation helpful but not required.
how_to_apply_tip: Early-career track fits a 0-3 yr postdoc exactly; read their research-area list and sign up to the newsletter, since rounds open with a pre-proposal stage.

name: Multi-Agent AI Safety Funding Call (Cooperative AI Foundation, Schmidt Sciences, Google DeepMind, ARIA)
amount: Tier 1 up to USD 300,000; Tier 2 USD 300,000-1,000,000
eligibility: Universities, research institutes, non-profits; independent researchers need a fiscal sponsor if selected
eligibility_note: Call page: 'Open globally'; non-US institutions can receive funds directly if 501(c)(3)-equivalent (verified via NGOSource).
how_to_apply_tip: Pakistani public universities usually need NGOSource equivalency determination; start that paperwork with your ORIC office well before the next round.

name: Internet Society Foundation Research Grant Programme
amount: Independent researchers up to USD 200,000; institutions up to USD 500,000
eligibility: Independent researchers with PhD/Master's and publications, or public universities/public research institutions; applied, open research on Inclusive/Green/Trustworthy Internet, meaningful connectivity
eligibility_note: Programme described as open to researchers and public institutions 'around the world'; private institutions not eligible; Foundation has funded multiple Pakistan projects. Check grantee eligibility/compliance document.
deadline: Annual - usually April-May (2026 round: 7 Apr-22 May)
how_to_apply_tip: Apply via a public university (private universities are ineligible as institutions) or as an independent PI; register in Fluxx at least 24h before deadline. AI angle: trustworthy internet / network measurement with ML.

name: Wikimedia Research Fund
amount: Type 1: USD 2,000-50,000; Type 2: up to USD 150,000 (max 75k/yr); Type 3 events up to USD 50,000
duration: Up to 12 months (Type 1/3); up to 24 months (Type 2)
eligibility: Individuals, groups, organisations; established researchers in Wikimedia research or wishing to enter it (NLP, ML, knowledge graphs fit well)
eligibility_note: No country restriction; welcomes 'all regions of the world' and particularly encourages Asia, Africa, Latin America, Eastern Europe.
deadline: Annual - LOI usually mid-January (2026 cycle: LOI 16 Jan, full proposal 3 Apr)
how_to_apply_tip: Strong fit for Urdu/regional-language NLP on Wikipedia/Wikidata; use the program's 1:1 office hours before the January LOI.

name: APNIC Foundation Research Fellowships
amount: USD 10,000 stipend
eligibility: Residents of APNIC service region; master's+ degree, 7-10 years field experience, at least one first-author peer-reviewed paper; tracks incl. Sustainable AI, DPI, Internet infrastructure
eligibility_note: Must reside in one of 56 APNIC service-region economies; Pakistan (PK) is listed under South Asia on the service-region page.
deadline: Annual - usually March (2026 round closed 31 Mar 2026)
how_to_apply_tip: The 7-10 years experience bar may count PhD research years; apply in the Sustainable AI track with a policy-relevant output.

name: ISIF Asia Grants
eligibility: Organisations (government, private, NGO incl. universities) registered in APNIC service region; Internet-for-development projects
eligibility_note: Lead organisation must be registered in one of 56 APNIC economies; Pakistan is in the service region. Individuals cannot apply.
deadline: Annual - concept notes usually late March-April (2027 round expected)
how_to_apply_tip: Apply through your university/ORIC as the lead organisation; frame an AI-enabled connectivity or community-network project.

name: Emergent Ventures
amount: See website (fellowships/grants, typically small)
eligibility: Anyone 13+ worldwide with high-impact 'zero to one' ideas; no credentials required
eligibility_note: Supports 'thinkers and doers worldwide'; no country restriction stated (dedicated tranches for India, Africa, etc.).
how_to_apply_tip: Short, punchy application; AI-written applications are explicitly not accepted. Pitch an ambitious AI project with societal impact.

name: Cosmos Institute Grants (AI for Truth-Seeking & Human Autonomy)
amount: Typically USD 1,000-10,000 (cash + Prime Intellect compute credits); larger for exceptional proposals
eligibility: Builders/researchers prototyping AI that strengthens human autonomy and truth-seeking; no credentials required
eligibility_note: No formal nationality restriction published; program states anyone can apply.
how_to_apply_tip: Fill the 'Express interest in future rounds' form now; proposals should be a concrete working prototype buildable in 90 days.

name: COMSTECH-TWAS Joint Research Grants for Young Scientists in OIC
amount: Up to USD 15,000 (equipment, consumables, literature; no salaries/travel)
eligibility: OIC nationals with PhD, early-career, generally under 40, at a university/research institution in an OIC country; fields include IT and computer sciences
eligibility_note: COMSTECH page: 'nationals of OIC Member States ... working at a university or research institution in an OIC country'. Pakistan is an OIC member and COMSTECH host.
how_to_apply_tip: Program page looks dated (2017 stats); email COMSTECH (comstech@comstech.org) to confirm the current cycle. Cannot apply to TWAS Research Grants in same year.

name: COMSTECH-IFS Research Grants Programme
amount: Typically USD 7,000-15,000 per project (2021-23 awards)
eligibility: Early-career scientists in OIC member states; historically agriculture/environment/food sciences
eligibility_note: Pakistan listed among funded countries (49 grantees, USD 559,834 cumulative 1998-2023).
how_to_apply_tip: Fits AI applied to agriculture/water/food (e.g. image-based crop disease detection, as in a 2023 Pakistani award). Note: ifs.se domain no longer belongs to IFS; confirm the current IFS call channel via COMSTECH.

name: OIC-COMSTECH Research Grant Program for Young Women Researchers
amount: USD 5,000-7,000 per project
eligibility: Young women researchers from OIC member states (women only)
eligibility_note: Open to young women researchers from OIC member states; Pakistan is an OIC member.
deadline: Annual - usually around April (2025-26 round closed 06 Apr 2026)
how_to_apply_tip: Only relevant if the applicant is female; 690 proposals in last round, so keep the budget tight and the deliverables specific.

name: Science of Trustworthy AI RFP
amount: Tier 1 up to USD 1M; Tier 2 USD 1-5M (indirects capped 10%)
eligibility: Individual researchers or teams at universities/research institutions, including international institutions
eligibility_note: FAQ (draft) lists international institutions as eligible subject to 501(c)(3)-equivalency evaluation.
how_to_apply_tip: Large grants; best approached as co-PI with an international collaborator. Start NGOSource equivalency early.

name: AI2050 Early Career Fellowship
amount: Up to USD 300,000 (per Schmidt Sciences)
eligibility: Postdoctoral and pre-tenure researchers from around the world; nomination only
eligibility_note: Fellows page: aimed at researchers 'from around the world'; closed nomination process, no open application.
how_to_apply_tip: Cannot self-apply: ask your institution or senior collaborators connected to AI2050 to nominate you; build a visible beneficial-AI research agenda.

name: Internet Freedom Fund (incl. applied research)
eligibility: Individuals 18+ and organisations; technology or applied research projects helping people facing censorship/surveillance
eligibility_note: Open 'regardless of nationality'; only OFAC-sanctioned countries excluded (Pakistan is not).
how_to_apply_tip: Submit a concept note first (response in ~6-8 weeks); ML-based censorship measurement or deepfake/surveillance detection fits.

name: NLnet Foundation Open Calls (NGI Zero / Restack / CodeSupply funds)
amount: EUR 5,000-50,000 for a first grant
eligibility: Individuals or organisations doing open-source technical development (open licences required)
eligibility_note: Any country can apply, but EU-funded calls usually expect Horizon Europe-eligible applicants; others must justify a 'European dimension'.
how_to_apply_tip: Bimonthly deadlines; partner with a European collaborator or show EU user benefit. Proposal must be human-written (AI use disclosed).

name: SFF Funding Rolling Application / S-Process Grant Rounds
amount: Total USD 20-40M+ per year across rounds (per-grant varies)
eligibility: Charities or projects with a fiscal sponsor; individuals need a fiscal sponsor; AI safety among focus areas
eligibility_note: Nonprofits outside US-defined adversarial nations can generally apply; individuals cannot apply without a fiscal sponsor.
deadline: Rolling application; Main Round usually April
how_to_apply_tip: Secure a fiscal sponsor (e.g. a US/UK AI-safety nonprofit) first; rolling application also triggers a Speculation Grant request.

name: Career Development and Transition Funding
amount: See website
eligibility: People at any career stage transitioning into work on global catastrophic risks incl. AI safety (independent study, upskilling, transition periods)
eligibility_note: Official page returned 403 to automated fetch; secondary sources describe rolling, worldwide eligibility. Verify on official page.
how_to_apply_tip: Explain clearly how the funded period moves you into an AI safety research career; also check Coefficient Giving's technical AI safety RFP page for open calls.
